East Bay Regional Park District · November 2026
# Rebecca Lewington for East Bay Parks Director, Ward 3
Engineer, communicator, and 30-year parks user – for parks that balance conservation, recreation, and access for everyone.
Where I Stand About Rebecca
30years in our parks 30years in tech 15US patents Ward 3home turf
Who I Am
## A Parks Person, Through and Through
For 30 years I've hiked and biked the East Bay's regional parks – they're where I walk my dog, take my photographs, and clear my head. I'm running for the Park District Board because I want the parks we love to thrive for the next generation: resilient against climate change and wildfire, welcoming to every community, and managed with care and common sense.
I spent 30 years as an engineer and communicator in the IT and semiconductor industries – building products, leading teams, and translating complicated problems into plain language. That's the job of a Park District director: listen carefully, weigh the evidence, and explain the decision honestly.
My Experience

On the trail
## Thirty years on these trails
Riding, hiking, and building them.
Priorities
## What I'll Work For
Four priorities guide how I'd serve on the Board – drawn from decades in the parks, not from politics.
01
### Climate Resilience
Mitigating the effects of climate change on our parks – tree mortality, sea level rise, and wildfire prevention – with reforestation, native vegetation restoration, and pragmatic fuels management.
02
### Parks for All
Expanding equitable access for all communities and abilities – better outreach, transportation connections, educational programs, and recreation opportunities, so more people see the parks as theirs.
03
### Financial Stewardship
Strong, transparent stewardship of taxpayer resources – a pragmatic mix of bonds, climate-resilience grants, philanthropy, and fair fees that go visibly back into the facilities people use.
04
### Conservation & Recreation
The District works because protecting nature and connecting people to it reinforce one another. I'll keep that balance – conservation and recreation as partners, not opponents.
I need your help to win this race! It will cost a lot to connect with the 240,000 voters in Ward 3. Please contribute what you can by clicking the “Donate” button above. I am not accepting contributions from developers, fossil fuel interests, or anyone whose interests run counter to the well-being of our parks and visitors. When I vote on the Board, the only interest I'll owe is yours. Questions? ebrpd-ward3@rebeccalewington.com
Skin in the Game
## I Show Up for the Parks
Loving the parks is easy. Maintaining them is work – and I do the work: volunteer trail days like the Bay Area Ridge Trail Day of Service at Crockett Hills, crew-lead training at Joaquin Miller, tools in hand alongside the people who keep these trails alive.
That's the perspective I'll bring to the Board: not just what the parks look like from a trailhead sign, but what they take to maintain – and how much more we could do with a stronger volunteer network behind them.
My Volunteering Answer
Straight Answers
## Ask Me Anything
Where do I stand on wildfire management? On trails and mountain bikes? On how Measure WW money should be spent? I've answered the questions candidates actually get asked – in writing, in plain language, with my reasoning shown.
The Q&A grows as new questions come in. If yours isn't there yet, it will be.
Read the Q&A
Join us!
## Want to get involved?
Subscribe to campaign updates, or volunteer to help get the word out: host a yard sign, hand out door hangers, talk to park users.
This Sunday, October 11: walk with Rebecca, 9 AM in Hayward. Details and RSVP →
Join the mailing list Volunteer
## Election Day: November 3, 2026
The East Bay Regional Park District Board decides how 126,000 acres of public land are cared for. Ward 3 deserves a director who knows the parks from the trail, not just the boardroom.

Our parks are some of the most beautiful places in the East Bay, and they are essential community assets for families from every background. Rebecca Lewington understands that protecting our open spaces and ensuring equitable access must go hand in hand. Her track record of thoughtful problem-solving, commitment to public service, and dedication to making our parks welcoming for everyone make her the right leader for the East Bay Regional Park District Board. I’m proud to support Rebecca Lewington for Director.
Assemblymember Buffy WicksCalifornia State Assembly, District 14
I'm endorsing Rebecca Lewington for East Bay Regional Park District Director, Ward 3. Why? Because she's the right person for the job! She'll work well with the board and the dedicated staff who make our parks special. Rebecca has the experience, values, and vision needed to protect our open spaces while ensuring everyone in our communities has access to them. She will be a strong voice for our parks and for the East Bay families who rely on them. I hope you'll join me in supporting Rebecca's campaign.
Assemblymember Liz OrtegaCalifornia State Assembly, District 20
